notes:
mangoclass 2.0.

**Google Classroom.** Sign in with the account you pick, and the panel shows what is due, what is turned in and what came back marked.

**PowerSchool.** Your grades, your GPA and your classes, read from the student portal in the same session you would be looking at it in.

**The student weekly.** Point it at the school's week-at-a-glance and it reads the whole week — every day's classes, their rooms and their times — and works out which days are the same letter and which slot holds a different class each week.

**Sync between your own computers.** Hand a schedule from one Mac to another over the local network. Nothing leaves your network.

**Settings has a sidebar**, so everything above has somewhere to live.

**A command-line mangoclass** for Linux and Windows, reading the same schedule.json the app writes: `mangoclass today`, `mangoclass week`, `mangoclass now --date "2026-09-14 09:30"`.

**Fixed:** a rotating-class rule that could not find its slot by name fell back to counting from the end of the day and renamed whatever was sitting there, which on a timetable with a single support block meant the last core lesson of the day came back under the wrong name. A rule that cannot find its slot now leaves the day alone.
